Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks — answers below and a couple of concrete asks ahead of the tech call.

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering
   - PrivateLink: Supported in both us-west-2 and us-east-1. Recommended when you want endpoint-level security and minimal routing changes. Works cross-account and is a good fit if you want to avoid managing BGP/routing.
   - VPC Peering: Also supported. Requires standard route table updates in your account and ours; it’s typically quicker for intra-account setups. Peering does not support transitive routing, so consider if your architecture uses central transit VPCs.

2) Routing and managed options
   - We don’t push routes into your VPC automatically. For peering, you’ll add the peering route to the relevant route tables. For PrivateLink, we provide an interface endpoint you create in your subnet — no route table changes required.

3) IP allowlists and egress ranges
   - For allowlists we can provide a short list of managed IPs for the interface endpoints (PrivateLink) or a stable set of egress IPs for Dedicated/hosted egress after a provisioning window. We will provide the exact CIDR blocks 48 hours before the scheduled cutover/testing window.

4) On-prem / air-gapped
   - We do offer an on-prem deployment package for air-gapped environments; that usually moves the conversation into our Private + on-prem track and has a slightly different provisioning timeline. Happy to introduce our Private deployments PM if that looks like your path.

Pre-call asks (to help Neha/Logan scope the environment):
- Can you share an internal network diagram (subnets, NAT/egress, transit VPCs) and a list of source IPs (or ranges) that will need to reach our endpoints?
- Do you have any specific firewall/proxy rules that inspect TLS that we should account for?

I’ve attached the networking checklist and MAP for your security team.
